milestones.label: Daily time playing games or using a computer for leisure
milestones.population: the population interviewed for the American Time Use Survey, whose age universe begins in the mid-teens, averaged across all days of the year
whatChanges: Games and computer leisure take up more of an average day in the late teen band than in any other age band the survey publishes.
This is one slice of leisure time, counted alongside television, reading, socializing and everything else people do with unpaid hours.
These are averages across a population and across every day of the week, not a description of any one person's week.
milestones.notes: The band named here is the youngest the survey publishes, so the window begins where the survey's age universe begins rather than at a measured start.

milestones.label: Daily time spent relaxing and thinking in the early adult band
milestones.population: the population interviewed for the American Time Use Survey, averaged across all days of the year, in the single age band the article names
whatChanges: Time counted as relaxing and thinking, rather than as any other activity, takes up less of an average day in this band than in the older bands the article names.
Relaxing and thinking is the survey's own category and does not include sleep, television or socializing, which are counted separately.
These are averages across a population and across every day of the week, not a description of any one week.
milestones.notes: The window is the age band the article names and nothing wider. The bands the article does not name are not described here at all.

milestones.label: Daily time spent relaxing and thinking in the band before the oldest
milestones.population: the population interviewed for the American Time Use Survey, averaged across all days of the year, in the single age band the article names
whatChanges: Time counted as relaxing and thinking takes up more of an average day in this band than in the early adult band, and less than in the oldest band the article names.
The same sentence reports time spent socializing and communicating for this band, and that figure is higher here than in the oldest band.
These are averages across a population and across every day of the week, not a description of any one week.
milestones.notes: The window is the age band the article names and nothing wider.

milestones.label: Daily time spent relaxing and thinking in the oldest band the article names
milestones.population: the population interviewed for the American Time Use Survey, averaged across all days of the year, in the oldest age band the article names
whatChanges: Time counted as relaxing and thinking takes up more of an average day in this band than in either younger band the article names.
Time spent socializing and communicating is reported as slightly lower here than in the band just below it.
These are averages across a population and across every day of the week, not a description of any one week.
milestones.notes: The article's oldest band is open-ended at the top, so the window closes at this timeline's own ceiling rather than at a measured end. The sentence carrying this band's figure says the two activities take about the same time "each", and its antecedent is the sentence about the band below, which is why that source is carried here too.

milestones.label: Daily time spent reading for personal interest in the early twenties
milestones.population: the population interviewed for the American Time Use Survey, averaged across all days of the year, with reading counted only when it is done for personal interest rather than for school or paid work
whatChanges: Reading chosen for its own sake takes up less of an average day in this band than in any other band the article names.
Reading done for school or for paid work is counted elsewhere and does not appear in this figure.
These are averages across a population and across every day of the week, not a description of any one week.
milestones.notes: The window is the age band the article names and nothing wider. Until the fix pass this record ran from this band to the oldest one it was being compared with, so a true figure about the oldest band rendered beside every year in between.

milestones.label: Belonging to a community, civic or religious organization across adult life
milestones.researchNote: Needed: a verbatim sentence naming an age band together with the share of people who belong to a group or organization. Candidates to fetch: the AmeriCorps Volunteering and Civic Life in America pages on americorps.gov, whose organizational membership measure is published by demographic group but which refused an automated fetch in this pass; the Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement detailed tables on census.gov; the AmeriCorps open data dashboard on data.americorps.gov, if it publishes a sentence rather than a table alone. The Pew religious attendance report was fetched and its narrative names older and younger adults without giving an age band beside a figure, so it cannot resolve this.
milestones.windowInWords: Belonging to a congregation, a club, a union, a neighborhood group or another organization is often described as more common in the later adult years than in the earliest, but no source fetched in this pass gave a verbatim sentence naming an age band beside a figure, so no window is asserted.
